Black Myth: Wukong is a compelling soulslike/action game, however, I personally had a few issues with the game. 

The story is set after the journey to the west, but I found it confusing to follow for the most part. 

Level design peaked for me in the second location and steadily declined thereafter. Levels follow a very linear pattern but don't feel particularly rewarding for exploring the few side paths as most of the time you will find upgrade materials that you end up having an abundance of by the end of the game anyway.

The bosses felt like a quantity over quality situation. The major bosses are very well designed and were frankly really cool, but the other 80% of bosses felt like fodder and didn't really do much for me. There is also a major difficulty difference between every single boss except for the final boss and the [spoiler] secret boss [/spoiler], which feels inconsistent.

Overall I give the game a 6.5/10, I do recommend it as the experience is quite good, but I wouldn't be urging anyone to pick it up as a must play.

Black Myth: Wukong is honestly one of the most impressive games I've played. The visuals are incredible, the world is beautifully designed, and the boss fights are easily one of the best parts of the game. Every fight feels different, and while some bosses can be frustratingly difficult, finally beating them feels so rewarding. The combat is smooth, the environments are full of detail, and the whole Chinese mythology-inspired setting makes the game feel special. It's not a perfect game, but the overall experience is absolutely worth it. Definitely a game I'd recommend playing at least once.

Black Myth: Wukong was one of the biggest surprises I've played in recent years. Going in, I expected a solid action game, but what I got was a visually stunning adventure packed with memorable boss fights and incredible set pieces.

The combat is easily the highlight of the game. It's fast, satisfying, and gives you plenty of abilities and transformations to experiment with. While many compare it to Souls games, I found it more accessible and focused on spectacle rather than frustration. The boss battles are some of the best I've experienced in an action RPG, and every major victory feels earned.

Visually, the game is absolutely breathtaking. The environments are rich with detail, the creature designs are fantastic, and the Unreal Engine 5 visuals truly shine. Playing in 4K was a treat, with many moments that looked straight out of a CGI movie.

The story, inspired by Journey to the West, is intriguing and full of mystery. While some parts can be difficult to follow if you're unfamiliar with the source material, the atmosphere, cutscenes, and world-building kept me invested from start to finish.

Performance-wise, the game ran surprisingly well. I experienced only minor stutters here and there, and overall the experience was smooth and polished.

Bottom line: Black Myth: Wukong proves that Chinese developers are absolutely cooking right now. The level of quality, ambition, and attention to detail on display here is incredible, especially for a studio's first AAA title. It may not reinvent the genre, but it delivers stunning visuals, excellent combat, and unforgettable boss encounters. If you're a fan of action games, this is an easy recommendation. I thoroughly enjoyed it. 🔥🐒🎮

it took me 66h to 100% the game and i definitely have some thoughts

The game is visually stunning with or without ray tracing (i played without), the environments feel alive, the sound design helps bring it all together and immerse you fully into the game. 
The enemies are tough but you always feel like you are learning and not a single enemy felt unfair (Except Earlang, f that guy) and with enough tries you will beat them, im fairly new to the souls like genre and i could beat the game fairly easily so i dont think its too difficult, which is good. 
The story is quite confusing at times, or maybe its because i played the game over multiple weeks but the combat was so much fun that i honestly didnt really pay too much attention to it.
There are quests and missable things in the game which are not explicitly stated anywhere and you only understand with clues from dialogue (i used a checklist since its easier especially since there is no way i can beat the game 100% in one sitting) but i see this as a positive and it incentivizes exploration.

Now some of the bad
Some places that look like you can walk over/trough are blocked by invisible walls (not super common but i did get stuck in a few places in Ch4).
if you get close to ledges that you are able to jump off, it will automatically make you jump, meaning some parts of the game with tight bridges are super annoying because a slight misstep will make you jump off and die.
Sometimes id get random visual glitches that would fix themselves in a few seconds but it would mess with vision
Sound would cut out if tp to a shrine to farm enemies.
Speaking of RNG drops, i got very lucky and pretty much got all RNG drops in about 20-30 mins of farming but ive seen some people having to farm for hours, this for me takes away from the game a bit as i want to explore not hit the same guy for 20mins straight.
The Pagoda part of Ch3 does not have enough save points, especially with the debuffs on my first playthrough it took me about as much time to beat Pagoda as it did the rest of the chapter, some people might enjoy it but for me it was the worst part of the game.
Some Achievements would not pop properly so i had to do alot of extra boss fighting in NG+ purely due to the achievement not working. 

I did not touch the Challenge modes, though they are there and give some special weapons, but as it was not needed for 100% and im not super into tournament style battles i left it alone.

Overall a great experience that im glad i came back to finish, i started the game back in 2024 shortly after release and did not enjoy it at all, but today i can say that it is worth a play and has inspired me to look into the books that this game is based upon.
